patterns.rationale: Anchors on the canonical A=1..Z=26 letter-ordinal convention declaration. The attacker must declare the encoding scheme for the agent to decode it; this declaration is the reliable signal. Covers any tool name encoded this way, not just get_env.
patterns.fp_notes: Could theoretically appear in a math or cipher education document, but not plausible in agent-facing content.

patterns.rationale: The NATO phonetic attack must instruct the agent how to extract the tool name. "Taking the leading character of each term" is the extraction instruction — narrow, unambiguous, and has no plausible benign occurrence in API/agent documents.
patterns.fp_notes: Could appear in linguistics or typography docs; not in agent-runtime content.

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 declares its encoding scheme as "decimal ASCII ordinals" — a phrase that appears verbatim as the scheme label. An attacker using this technique must name it or provide equivalent instruction; this anchors on the naming form.
patterns.fp_notes: Appears in character encoding tutorials, but those do not also instruct an agent to "concatenate to retrieve the handle."

patterns.rationale: Covers both Miss 3's "convert each value to its corresponding ASCII character" and Miss 5's "convert each two-character hex pair to its corresponding ASCII character" — the imperative decoding instruction is the distinguishing signal. Catches the hex-encoding variant (Miss 5) that the narrower "decimal ASCII ord" pattern does not.
patterns.fp_notes: "Convert a value to ASCII" appears in encoding tutorials; the `each` quantifier and full imperative form narrows it significantly.

patterns.rationale: Miss 6's interleaving attack requires instructing the agent to extract characters at specific positional offsets. "Odd-indexed, one-based" and "collecting characters at positions 1, 3, 5…" are the extraction-instruction signals. Extends FLIP_ATTACK since this is character-level transformation to hide content — the same conceptual family as read-backwards.
patterns.fp_notes: "Odd-indexed" appears in DSP/signal processing; the co-occurrence with "one-based" or "collecting characters" makes it agent-content-specific.

semantic_note: N/A — each miss carries a distinctive encoding-scheme declaration or decoding-instruction phrase that regex can anchor on.
